official_measurement_examples.name: Important Areas current dataset
official_measurement_examples.fact: Defra's Noise Action Planning Important Areas Round 3 dataset was updated 1 July 2026 and identifies areas for noise-action planning; an Important Area is not an automatic planning refusal zone.

official_measurement_examples.name: Model year versus update date
official_measurement_examples.fact: Round 3 road-noise products can be republished or metadata-updated in 2026 while their underlying strategic mapping analysis is from an earlier reference year; dataset update date must not be treated as measurement date.

official_measurement_examples.name: Modelled grid limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Round 3 road-noise layers use modelled noise classes on a 10 metre grid at a 4 metre receptor height; polygon class is not an on-site acoustic measurement at a proposed façade or garden.

official_measurement_examples.name: Metric separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Lnight, LAeq16h, Lden and octave-band outputs are different indicators and averaging periods and must not be silently interchanged as one noise value.

official_measurement_examples.name: Round 4 context
official_measurement_examples.fact: Newer Round 4 products can use different source years and outputs, so Round 2, Round 3 and Round 4 datasets must retain their individual lineage rather than being merged as equivalent measurements.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning relevance
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning guidance requires noise to be considered where development creates noise or is sensitive to the existing and anticipated acoustic environment; mapped exposure alone does not determine the planning balance.

official_measurement_examples.name: Permit noise assessment
official_measurement_examples.fact: Environment Agency permit guidance updated 12 May 2026 governs noise and vibration assessment for regulated activities and is separate from land-use planning permission and planning-condition assessment.

official_measurement_examples.name: Parcel limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Strategic noise layers do not establish title, exact façade exposure, mitigation feasibility, indoor levels, planning permission or final parcel development yield.

core_rules: Noise Important Area is not automatic planning refusal
strategic noise map is model evidence not site measurement
dataset publication/update date is not necessarily acoustic model year
Lnight and LAeq16h are distinct metrics
Lden and octave-band outputs remain distinct
Round2 Round3 and Round4 lineage must remain separate
model receptor height and grid resolution must be retained
environmental-permit noise assessment is distinct from planning permission
permit compliance is not planning permission
noise map does not determine land ownership
noise polygon does not determine development yield
absence from Important Areas is not proof of quiet conditions
no parcel acoustic clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Official Defra, Environment Agency, National Data Library, GOV.UK and legislation.gov.uk sources checked on 2026-07-26. May-July 2026 dataset/permit updates were retained with model-year, metric, mapping-round, planning and permit separation; no parcel promotion.
